$comment: THE BUNDLED DEFAULT, not the only source. See presets/README.md for the resolution chain:
plugin options -> ~/.config/lacode/pool.json -> this file -> a built-in fallback.
src/lib/pool.ts reads it at config time and rewrites every pooled variant agent
(explore-N, implement-N, context-N) plus the provider whitelists
to match, so no model is written down next to an agent anywhere.
Slot N is the same model for every base agent, which is what makes load shared.
RULES, all validated at startup: models are written provider/model-id, split on the FIRST
slash only so openrouter's vendor-prefixed ids (nvidia/x:free) resolve; must be distinct.
AT MOST 4 SLOTS: one hidden variant per base per slot is declared, so a fifth entry would
route at an agent that does not exist. Extra entries are dropped with a warning.
WEIGHT IS THE ONLY KNOWN KNOB: one position per unit of weight in the rotation run,
and a concurrency ceiling of TWICE that weight -- a share of the work, not a priority.
Routing is ORDER-FIRST
WEIGHTED ROUND-ROBIN: the slot list is walked IN ORDER and each slot takes as many
consecutive turns as its weight says, so weights 3,2,1,1 produce the run 1,1,1,2,2,3,4,
which then repeats. The rule is:
1. a persistent cursor in the pool directory marks where in that run the next spawn
lands, so every opencode process on the machine shares one rotation
2. a turn is SKIPPED only when its slot is cooling or already at its ceiling, and the
rotation resumes at the following turn
3. once EVERY slot is at its ceiling, the overflow goes to the least loaded slot,
so a burst past the summed ceilings degrades to even spreading and never blocks
With this file: big-pickle takes 3 consecutive turns, then minimax-m3.1-flash-free
(opencode-go) takes 2, then deepseek-v4.1-flash-free and glm-5.3-flash-free take 1
Equal weights give a plain round robin in list order. 2,2,1,1 reproduces the old
primary/overflow cycle exactly, which is why the old tier values still work.
WEIGHTS DESCEND, AND THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. The rotation is order-first: the run is
expanded in declaration order, so the heaviest slot must come first for a skip to
land on the heaviest slot that is LEFT. A heavier slot declared after a lighter one
is unreachable in the way the pool means.
EVERY SLOT IS A MODEL THAT IS PROBABLY STILL THERE NEXT WEEK, AND NO TWO SLOTS
SHARE A FAMILY. A free model can be withdrawn by its provider without warning --
space-bunny-free was pulled from the opencode provider while it was still this
file's first slot, and every new session then died on 'Model not found'. So the
slots here are the long-lived free ones (big-pickle has been on the opencode
provider for years), spread over two providers and four model families, because a
pool where every slot is one family is one withdrawal away from being empty. If a
slot does go away, the plugin warns at startup and the rest keep working; the fix
is a one-line edit here, not a redesign.
Round-robin rather than heaviest-first because re-prioritising the heaviest slot on
EVERY spawn drained the fastest provider's free-tier window early: one provider
absorbed all work up to its ceiling and kept being refilled the moment a claim
completed, while the other slots sat idle -- until the fast provider hit its limit and
its 429s displaced every agent type at once. Every slot a turn per cycle puts a fast
slot with a large usage window to work early in the cycle while it is still fast, and
no provider's quota sits unused while another's is drained.
Absent means weight 1. Must be a number in (0, 100]; anything else warns and uses 1.
List order sets the rotation for every slot, not just a tie-break: earlier positions
take their turns earlier in each cycle, so put the slots you want worked first at the
top of the list.
COST IS THE DEFAULT, NOT A CONSTRAINT. These four slots are free because that is what
the pool is FOR: mechanical work -- reading files, grepping, mechanical edits, cartography.
They are not here to be the smartest model in the system. The point of putting that work
on a near-free model is that the mechanical tokens stop being spent by your expensive
main model, and that the main model's context is never filled with file contents it does
not need to reason about. Those are two separate effects and the second is the larger one.
The pool is OPEN: it accepts any model you give it, free, cheap or expensive, and the
plugin never inspects, prices, warns about, filters or rewrites one. There is no
allowlist, no cost check, and no validation beyond structure (US-7). Free is expressed
once, right here, as the choice this file makes for you when you have not made one.
You MAY substitute your own list, including paid models, and nothing will reject or
second-guess it: edit the "slots" array below (replace a {"model": ...} entry with your
own provider/id and keep the weight), or leave this file alone entirely and put the list
in ~/.config/lacode/pool.json instead, which wins over it.
Re-check any model you substitute against models.dev; this project does not look prices
up at runtime and will not guess at them for you.
Changing this file requires restarting every opencode process: plugins are not hot-reloaded.
